interview.answer: Native controls vary across browsers and can be hard to read or tap; styling improves usability and consistency.

interview.q: What is the first rule of accessible forms?
interview.answer: Every input has a visible, associated label.

interview.q: How do you associate a label with an input?
interview.answer: Use the for attribute matching the input's id, or nest the input inside the label.
It groups related controls, such as radio buttons, with a legend describing the group.
The caption for a fieldset, read by screen readers as the group name.

interview.q: How do you style a focus state accessibly?
interview.answer: Provide a visible outline or ring with sufficient contrast, and never remove focus styles without a replacement.

interview.q: What is :focus-visible good for in forms?
interview.answer: It keeps keyboard focus visible while hiding rings after mouse clicks.

interview.q: What is appearance: none on inputs?
interview.answer: It removes native styling so you can build a custom control, but you must restyle all states.

interview.q: How does accent-color affect form controls?
interview.answer: It tints checkboxes, radio buttons and progress bars without replacing native styling.

interview.q: How do you style the text input caret?
interview.answer: Use caret-color to match the caret to the brand or theme.
Use ::placeholder to change colour and opacity, but keep enough contrast for readability.

interview.q: Why should placeholders not replace labels?
interview.answer: Placeholders disappear on input, leaving no instruction, which hurts usability and accessibility.
A label that moves from inside the input to above it when the field has a value or focus.
Use :valid and :invalid to give visual feedback, but avoid showing errors before the user has finished.
It matches an invalid control only after the user has interacted with it, avoiding premature errors.
It matches a valid control after interaction, useful for positive feedback.
An attribute indicating an error; pair it with a visible message for screen readers.

interview.q: What is a form error message pattern?
interview.answer: Associate the input with the message using aria-describedby and move focus to the first error.
An attribute that hints the browser to fill values, improving speed and reducing errors.
It hints the virtual keyboard type, such as numeric or email.

interview.q: What is a select styling challenge?
interview.answer: Native select dropdowns are hard to style; appearance: none plus a custom arrow is common but must preserve accessibility.
A visually hidden native input paired with a styled label, keeping the native control for accessibility.

interview.q: What is a custom radio button?
interview.answer: Similar to a custom checkbox, using a hidden input and styled label while preserving keyboard behaviour.
A toggle styled as a switch, usually a checkbox with custom visuals and ARIA role switch.
An input type range styled with ::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb.
A bar showing task completion, styleable with ::-webkit-progress-bar and ::-moz-progress-bar.
A scalar gauge, styleable in some browsers but with limited control.
A contained block with padding, border or shadow, used to group related content.
An overlay dialog that blocks interaction with the page until dismissed.

interview.q: How do you centre a modal?
interview.answer: Use a flex or grid container with place-items: center, or fixed positioning with transform.
The dimmed area behind a modal, often a pseudo-element or separate div.
A high value above page content, but within a stacking context to avoid conflicts.
A small label that appears on hover or focus to explain an element.

interview.q: What is the accessibility risk of hover-only tooltips?
interview.answer: Keyboard and touch users may never see them; use focus and click triggers too.
A transient message that appears and disappears automatically, usually fixed in a corner.

interview.q: When is a skeleton screen better than a spinner?
interview.answer: When you can preview the layout of incoming content to reduce perceived load time.
A rotating indicator showing that an action is in progress.
A small label showing a count or status, often positioned on a corner of an icon.
A compact element representing an input, attribute or action, often removable.
A navigation trail showing the current location within a hierarchy.
A control that switches between panels of content without leaving the page.
A vertically stacked set of headers that reveal or hide associated content.
A list of options that appears on click or hover, often positioned absolutely.

interview.q: What is a responsive form layout?
interview.answer: A form that stacks fields on small screens and uses columns on larger ones.
A CSS grid that aligns labels and inputs across rows for a tidy form.
